segments.text: [Music] agile approaches are designed to help
you get value to your customers quickly while keeping your development work
aligned with business needs in order to maintain this alignment Agile Release
planning is conducted we serves as a way to bring the company vision and product
roadmap in the same room with the people who actually be executing on it release
planning helps agile teams plan how they'll execute on strategic yearly
plans of vision and roadmap and these mid-range plans in turn inform the more
immediate iteration and daily planning we collectively refer to these
activities as the five levels of planning each level helps teams
successfully work toward delivering value the concept of Agile Release
planning can be confusing because release is a loaded term usually it's
associated with releasing to production or the customer however in this context
we're referring to a time box we're planning for a period of time that
contains specific goals and deliverables that are to be achieved by the team
the team might deliver to production at the end of the time box or it might not
or it might deliver daily throughout the time box
in this case release planning merely refers to a Cadence
many teams conduct release planning quarterly for example
the release planning meeting is an opportunity for the team to make a
commitment to the completion of the highest ranked product backlog item for
the upcoming time box it also gives the team a chance to
synchronize on objectives and understand the bigger picture of their work to get
started you need a ranked product backlog which is responsibility of the
product owner in advance of the release planning meeting the product owner works
with the stakeholders and the delivery team to write user stories and rank the
backlog so that can be successfully delivered you also need a vision and
roadmap that reflects the market and your organizational objectives
we've found that successful release planning meetings all follow a similar
agenda that ensures connection to strategy collaboration and a realistic
plan the meeting kicks off the review of the vision and roadmap so everyone is on
the same page about the overall goal of the product
the team then reviews the architecture and any important technical information
in order to understand the technology Baseline for the release a release name
and theme is determined to help the team coalesce around a goal
while providing Focus for reviewing the user stories a review of the team's
velocities conducted as well as a review of the iteration schedule for this
release this lets us understand how much work
will be in the release and how to best distribute it across its iterations
it's also important for the team to review their definition of done
because the meeting will result in a commitment in work that can be done in
the time box the estimates need to be based on a shared definition of what it
means to be done it's at this point in the release planning meeting that the
product owner presents the user stories that are highest ranked in the backlog
and which should be the team's focus in the next release
the team reviews user stories and provides high level estimates typically
in the form of story points any store that is too big to be completed in a
single iteration needs to be broken down into small user stories so that it can
be distributed appropriately during this process the team will also be validating
the acceptance criteria so that everyone is clear on the work that needs to be
done once the distribution of stories across
all the iterations in the release has been completed the team should look back
and identify any issues concerns dependencies and assumptions that have
come up during the meeting release planning done well is more than just a
plan team develops a clear understanding of
its work and even begins to design together this team is ready to hit the
ground running and build the most valuable product increment this
